prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve action and garment-occlusion study. Produce a restrained twelve-figure sheet for the EXACT approved round pink Dango and tiny short fin-like hands in reference 1. Reference 2 is the current wardrobe identity only. Reference 3 is the approved canonical right-three-quarter body/face. No rejected four-legged/frog concept is included; do not invent one.
Layout: 3 rows × 4 columns on a plain light neutral background, equal character scale, full figures and generous spacing. Columns FRONT BARE, RIGHT-THREE-QUARTER BARE, FRONT DRESSED, RIGHT-THREE-QUARTER DRESSED. Rows WORKOUT, BUTTERFLY, CORNER. Small captions outside art only.
Preserve the approved exact round belly width-to-height ratio, tiny ears, small glossy eyes, tiny mouth, original two stub feet and restrained stepped outline/pink texture. Three-quarter has two eyes. No new tail anatomy, no new side lumps, no long arms, no fingers/toes/notches and no wide flattened frog torso.
WORKOUT: solve a small low-support pushing exercise that this compact anatomy can actually perform. Two modest forepaws support the body in front, close to the lower torso, while the two existing feet remain distinctly behind. Keep exactly two tiny hands and two original feet. Forepaws grow smoothly from the body without thin stems, closed oval shoulder roots, human wrists, elbow lines or long limbs. Their silhouette should remain compact and almost limbless, like the approved cup paws. Keep the round body recognizable with only a mild forward lean/lowering; do not widen it into a generic quadruped. Rear boots, when dressed, stay on actual rear feet partly behind the body/cape, not pasted on the front belly. Pink forepaws are not booted. Use the existing cream/navy exercise headband instead of straw hat during workout. Make the depth/contact relationship readable rather than exposing every far limb.
BUTTERFLY: a gentle chase key pose using the approved round body and short-foot locomotion, with a small lavender butterfly outside the face. Do not replace the approved gait with long running legs or a frog leap. Keep the character's tiny hands tucked or subtly visible; no big reaching arms.
CORNER: the same round creature mildly leaning inward and pretending to sleep, original tiny relaxed closed eyes and horizontal mouth. No laying-flat sleep redesign or new pillow/wall. Feet remain the original short feet, not added forepaws.
DRESSED: the existing narrow mint/lavender scarf, little brown boots, brown side satchel, lavender cape and, for butterfly/corner, small straw hat. Keep exact relative sizes and texture. Decide actual near/far occlusion with intact cloth over roots and little active paws in front only where necessary. Far clothes/feet may be hidden naturally. Hat crown/brim remain continuously seated around buried ear roots on the moving head, with zero exposed background wedge, no detached filler bridge and no ear tips through hat fabric. The brim must never hide an eye.
No gratuitous body shape or facial landmark changes, no 3D/vector restyling, no effects/scenery except the butterfly. The purpose is a bounded motion/depth design study using the approved tiny-paw character, not a new mascot.
